- `Plugins/P3/**`

- production Experience boots and reaches gameplay without V1 gameplay bootstrap

- architecture guard from A0 remains green against the final tree

## 2026-09-02 final product integration contract

**Current status: NOT READY.** This issue now owns the continuously runnable default product and its readiness ledger. ÔÇ£No feature expansionÔÇØ means no unrelated scope invention; it does not forbid implementing missing composition or behavior required by the existing North Star.

### Required default-path ledger

| Domain | Minimum closure state |
| --- | --- |
| Default map/GameMode/Experience | clean project-default boot; exact Experience/PawnData recorded |
| Player identity, input, camera | normal semantic input and view modes on the default path |
| Avatar and animation | authored package hydrated/valid, selected, spawned, and locomoting |
| Interaction, inventory, persistence | core loop and save/session behavior composed |
| Combat, abilities, traversal, VFX | normal-input server-authoritative loop with required presentation |
| Construction and earthworks | costs, world/navigation interaction, persistence, and multiplayer authority |
| Survival and respawn | cross-domain defeat/respawn state on the same product path |
| RTS, Lane War, tower defense, AI | coherent playable loop with one runtime authority |
| World/environment | production world boots without V1 repair/bootstrap ownership |
| UI/read models | integrated product state without central HUD scanning/switchboard |
| Multiplayer/session | dedicated server plus two clients for required networked loops |
| Presentation/performance | inspected current-head flows and recorded baseline |
| V1 retirement | one named authority per migrated system; V1 is reference/test only |

Every row records owner, exact head, state (`ABSENT`, `IMPLEMENTED`, `SYSTEM_PROVEN`, `DEFAULT_PATH_PROVEN`), proof level, and first unmet gate. Only `DEFAULT_PATH_PROVEN` satisfies this issue.

### Pull order and proof discipline

- Pull the oldest blocked default-path row; do not open more horizontal lanes while WIP or branch age rises.
- Validate LFS hydration, Primary Asset resolution, soft dependencies, authored metadata, and package loadability before build/runtime admission.
- Use one stable verifier and one default-product smoke per meaningful exact head.
- After the first exact failure, retry only after naming the source/content/environment/route change expected to invalidate it.
- Sealdiver selection and Grapple/Dash traversal are current observed examples, not substitutes for the full matrix.

Close only when all rows pass on one compatible head, required dedicated-server/two-client and inspected user-path evidence exists, and the final V1 single-authority audit passes.

## 2026-09-07 Tiny3D alignment and production asset admission
Current cross-repo authority is organicoverlords/tiny3d, especially its northstar/design update #375, authoring #372, rigging benchmark #373 and proof #13. Historical TinyLab links below are provenance, not a separate current product owner.

P3 owns materialization, profile/AnimBP/gameplay binding, physics/runtime cost and actual proof; Tiny3D owns source preparation/rigging and portable motion. Use #394 as the consumer executor and #2610 for complete match-state animation.

Stock Fox is excluded from inputs, donors, roster/benchmarks, qualification and fallbacks. Do not substitute stock or primitive placeholders for required user/generated asset proof. Preserve actual selected asset/variant identity and existing valid source/package work; newer unqualified content is a gap, not an automatic replacement.

Admission should surface missing/LFS-pointer content, incompatible skeleton/clip/profile, wrong axes/scale/materials, physics/collision gap and stale content/build identity before an expensive runtime attempt. Reuse merged #2429 materialization enforcement rather than recreating it.

Return exact package/mission/job/object/clip/runtime identities and the complete readable retained proof bundle through #394. Offline Tiny3D acceptance, P3 diagnostic playback and actual Lane War gameplay remain distinct. Update only the evidence invalidated by the changed source/rig/motion/consumer/capture input.

---

Cross-repo product aim: organicoverlords/TinyLab#77
Newest-content intake: organicoverlords/TinyLab#84

P3 is the real consumer/proof side of the Tiny3D asset lifecycle. The newest viable production assets and characters must not stop at Tiny3D packaging; they must be materialized into current P3/V2 and used through the intended gameplay/runtime paths.

Acceptance:
- Consume selected newest production assets/characters from verified Tiny3D identities/handoffs rather than creating an unrelated P3-only lineage.
- Preserve Tiny3D asset ID, handoff/package SHA-256 and mission identity in P3 materialization/result evidence.
- Record exact Unreal object/package paths actually created, reused or intentionally bound: StaticMesh/SkeletalMesh, Skeleton, AnimSequences, PhysicsAsset, materials/data assets and role-specific bindings as applicable.
- Prefer newest viable production replacements for current required P3 roles; explicitly mark older replaced content historical/superseded rather than using it for final milestone proof.
- Character/creature selections must be exercised through current V2 spawn/animation/movement/gameplay paths where their role requires it.
- Static/building/environment selections must be exercised through their real P3 render/collision/placement/destruction/earthworks path where applicable.
- Player-visible proof must use a genuine current rendered frame from the intended V2 runtime/world and be registered through the normal P3 milestone capture path.
- Legacy/showroom/network-smoke-only execution cannot satisfy current V2 player-facing proof.
- Return attributable materialization/runtime result receipts to Tiny3D so the library can expose P3_MATERIALIZED / P3_RUNTIME_PROVEN / failure state for the same asset identity.

Newest-content gate:
- Before final acceptance, compare selected P3 assets against the current newest viable source/library assets.
- If a newer intended replacement exists but is not Tiny3D-qualified and P3-proven, report it as an explicit gap rather than claiming coverage complete.
- At minimum, prove the newest viable character/creature plus representative newest static/environment/building/prop assets actually required by P3.

This issue is complete only when the selected newest assets are both present as canonical Tiny3D library assets and actively materialized/tested in P3; either half alone is incomplete.


## Newest-150 P3 consumption gate

P3 must consume the Tiny3D newest-150 production dataset rather than only a few hand-picked examples. Every selected asset required by a live P3 role must preserve its Tiny3D identity through Unreal materialization. The Tiny3D animation classification controls what P3 must exercise: walking/flying/swimming gameplay locomotion, cloth/fabric motion, tentacle/tail/appendage motion, feather/wing motion, foliage wind, rigid articulation, destruction or genuinely static behavior as applicable. Player-visible classified motion requires current rendered proof; a successful static import cannot satisfy an animation-required contract.


## Deterministic automatic consumer contract

P3 consumption is part of the unattended lifecycle, not a manual import ceremony. Given the same verified Tiny3D handoff and P3 version/configuration, the consumer must deterministically materialize or reuse the same intended Unreal objects/bindings, run the same role-qualified validation mission, and return hash-bound materialization/runtime proof without routine human sequencing.

Ambiguous Tiny3D semantics remain explicit gaps and must not be guessed by P3. Independent valid assets continue. Player-visible proof still requires the normal real V2 rendered-runtime evidence; automation is not permission to substitute logs/headless checks for visual acceptance.

The 100-asset bundle at `G:\Oma Drive\LowVRAM3D_asset_bundle_20260814` (9 categories: birds, characters, other_animals, other_assets, other_things, plants ├ù20, random_items, rocks, trees) plus the 389 entries already in `Content/Showroom/Static` are the raw material for populating the Lane War world. This issue is the p3 side of that: consuming qualified assets, not producing them.

**Route: through Tiny3D, not straight into p3.** That is the documented product boundary ÔÇö LowVRAM produces geometry and provenance, Tiny3D owns compilation, validation, qualification and the library, p3 is the downstream consumer that materializes and accepts at runtime. Importing bundle GLBs directly into `Content/` would skip qualification and put unvalidated meshes into the world with no way to answer later whether they passed anything.

Depends on organicoverlords/tiny3d#101 (unified hash-indexed library) and the materialization identity contract in organicoverlords/tiny3d#12.

Scope here:

1. Take the qualified set Tiny3D hands back, by content hash, not by filename.
2. Materialize into `Content/` under the existing showroom convention, recording the exact object/package path per asset so the identity contract round-trips.
3. Place them in the world ÔÇö `Content/Showroom/Maps/ALL_ASSETS_Lineup.umap` is the existing lineup for review; Lane War placement is the actual goal (see #413 base structures, #414 battlefield, #416 creeps).
4. Import in batches with GC between assets ÔÇö a bulk GLB import loop inside the editor OOMs it.
5. Acceptance is a rendered frame through `scripts/Invoke-P3VisualProofCapture.ps1`, not an import log. Assets present in the content browser is not the same claim as assets visible in the world.

Note for provenance: 17 of the assets already in `Content/Showroom/Static` have no surviving master PLY (deleted 2026-08-23). They are usable in their materialized form, but they cannot be regenerated at a different resolution or face budget without re-running generation from the source image.
